title: Square the readings
scenario: These readings are sorted smallest to biggest. Square each one — and keep them sorted.

intro.job: These readings are sorted smallest to biggest. Square each one — and keep them sorted.

idea.rule: The biggest square comes from the biggest number by size, not by sign — compare from both ends and fill from the back.
idea.detail: Squaring throws the sign away, so a big negative number makes a big square: (-4)² is 16. In a sorted list the biggest SIZES sit at the two ends. Put one finger on each end, compare their sizes with abs(), and the bigger one gives the biggest remaining square — write it into the last empty spot, then move that finger in.

watch.code:
n = len(nums)
squares = [0] * n
left, right = 0, n - 1
for pos in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    if abs(nums[left]) > abs(nums[right]):
        squares[pos] = nums[left] * nums[left]
        left += 1
    else:
        squares[pos] = nums[right] * nums[right]
        right -= 1
print(squares)

model_restatement: Square every reading and print the squares in sorted order.

clarify.question: Can I square them and then just sort?
clarify.answer: That works — but here, use the fact the input is already sorted: one pass, two fingers.

clarify.question: What if there are no readings?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Go through the readings in order, square each one, and add it to the answer. Print the answer.

why_line: Squaring in order keeps the input's order — but -4 is the biggest number by SIZE, so its square, 16, lands at the front of the list instead of near the end.

explain.rule: The readings are sorted by sign, but squares care about size — -4 is small as a reading and big as a square, so the order breaks at the very first number.
explain.bridge: So where in a sorted list do the biggest SIZES sit?

fix.rule: Two fingers at the ends: the one with the bigger size gives the next-biggest square, written into the answer from the back.

walk.gloss: Fill the answer from the last spot to the first.
Which end holds the bigger number by size?
The left one — its square goes in this spot, and the left finger moves in.
Otherwise the right one's square goes here, and the right finger moves in.

contrast.right: compare abs() at both ends, fill from the back
